_doc: Closed failure taxonomy for headless agent runs. Rules are tried in order; the first match wins. `level: run` codes make a run FAILED, `level: step` codes make it DEGRADED. `track: false` codes are recorded but never open an issue (normal agent exploration). A new code is added only when UNCLASSIFIED keeps recurring (open coding -> closed taxonomy). MAST/TRAIL columns map each code to the published taxonomies for comparison. `behavior` + `sites` name the harness behavior that owns each code and the files implementing it (references/handbook.md).

run_rules.when: auth_failed == true (run_agent.sh matched an auth error: expired OAuth session, invalid key, not logged in)
run_rules.fix: The `claude` login expired; every headless job fails until it is renewed. Run `claude` in a terminal and log in. The alarm (auth-alarm.json, Jarvis pill, one macOS notification) clears on the next good run.

run_rules.when: no JSON result, exit 143/SIGTERM, terminal_reason api_error, or is_error with no other run code
run_rules.fix: Usually transient (sleep, network, rate limit). Auth failures are AUTH_EXPIRED; recurring INFRA means the launchd environment is broken: check the job log.

run_rules.when: subtype error_max_turns / error_max_budget_usd, terminal_reason max_turns / budget_exhausted / prompt_too_long
run_rules.fix: Re-derive budget_usd from ledger p95 x 1.5 (see .claude/agents/<job>.md) or cut the batch the job is given.
The control spine stopped the run with checkpoints open: read the run's RESPONSE.md, find the box the agent could not clear.
The child never wrote its RESPONSE.md. Check the packet names the exact path and the agent definition's Success line.

step_rules.pattern: write-boundary guard|egress guard:|was blocked\. For security|outside the allowed (working )?director|outside the allowed zones
step_rules.fix: Agent wrote or listed outside the allowed zones (often /tmp), or outside its job's write_scopes (hook log line carries `job`). Zones: tell the agent definition to use its STATE_ROOT for scratch files. Scopes: if the path is a legitimate output of the job, a human widens `write_scopes:` in .claude/agents/<job>.md; otherwise the wall worked, fix the prompt. Egress guard: find what handed the agent that URL or query (hooks.jsonl carries `job` and `why`) and fix that source; never loosen the guard for one job.

step_rules.pattern: requires approval|Contains [a-z_ -]+|contains multiple operations|Parser skipped input|cannot be auto-allowed|integer attribute|Arithmetic expansion|Redirect has multiple targets|expansion obfuscation|has been denied|doesn't want to proceed|require explicit approval|Brace expansion|^(<tool_use_error>)?Blocked: |executes arbitrary commands
step_rules.fix: Headless runs cannot answer prompts. Either allowlist the exact command for that job (--allowedTools) or tell the agent to use Read/Grep/Glob and single plain commands instead of compound shell.

step_rules.pattern: Unknown skill|cannot be used with Skill tool
step_rules.fix: Repo skills are files, not Skill-tool skills. The agent must Read resources/skills/<category>/<slug>/SKILL.md.

step_rules.pattern: String to replace not found|has been modified since|has not been read yet|must read|Found \d+ matches of the string to replace
step_rules.fix: Agent edited from a stale or imagined copy, or anchored on a line that occurs more than once. Re-read before Edit; for append-only notes, append instead of replacing.
sites: the job's co-written files (e.g. PLAN.json via webapp/tasks.py)

step_rules.fix: The URL or query carried a shape research never needs (email address, encoded blob, oversized query). Tracking and token links are the usual cause: pass the agent the clean page URL. A deny on data that really was private means the guard worked; find out where the agent got it.

An `ls` found nothing. The Path rule tells agents to `ls` a folder before Read, so this is the rule working. Only act if one job's count climbs: that job has lost its paths, so treat it like PATH_MISS.

step_rules.pattern: File does not exist|EISDIR|No such file or directory|does not exist\.|ENOENT
step_rules.fix: Agent guessed a path. Put the exact paths it needs in the task packet or skill; prefer Glob before Read.
sites: the launcher's prompt and seeded files

step_rules.pattern: timeout of \d+ms|maxContentLength|went to sleep|ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|fetch failed|socket hang up|\b(403|404|429|5\d\d)\b.*(status|error)|Request failed|unable to fetch from|Request interrupted by user|search was cut off before any results
step_rules.fix: External site or sleep. A headless run has no user, so "Request interrupted by user" means the Mac slept (or the process was killed) mid-call. Only act if one host keeps failing: drop or replace that source.

step_rules.pattern: not installed|command not found|No module named|is not recognized
step_rules.fix: A dependency is missing on this Mac. Install it once (brew/uv) or remove the step that needs it.

step_rules.pattern: InputValidationError|Invalid tool parameters|tool_use_error>Error|ripgrep rejected the pattern
step_rules.fix: Malformed tool call. Usually model noise; recurring means a skill shows the wrong call shape.
A shell command returned non-zero (grep with no match counts). Exploration noise unless it hides a real step failure.

step_rules.when: assigned by scripts/quality.py, not by a tool error: a run of a listed job (daily-intel, meeting-prep) ended below a floor its own SKILL.md states (searches per section, item sources fetched, a prep and surface per meeting, task documents opened or carried, web-call cap)
step_rules.fix: The run finished clean but skipped work its skill requires. Read the signature (which floor), then the run next to one that met it (`pair QUALITY_FLOOR --job <job>`). The floor is prose the agent ignored, so the fix is a mechanism (a check script the run must pass, a seeded checklist), or a skill change if the floor itself is wrong.
